description.value: The study examined brain activation elicited by alcohol-associated and affectively positive, negative, and neutral pictures in detoxified alcohol-dependent subjects and healthy controls, and its association with subsequent relapse.

spans.text: Therefore, we measured brain activation elicited by alcohol-associated pictures and by standardized emotionally positive, negative, and neutral stimuli in detoxified alcoholic subjects and healthy control subjects.

value: a high relapse risk is associated with (1) increased brain activation during the presentation of alcohol-associated versus neutral stimuli in the prefrontal and cingulate cortex, striatum, and visual association centers, (2) decreased brain activation elicited by positive versus neutral stimuli in the brain reward system, particularly the ventral striatum/nucleus accumbens, and (3) increased amygdala activation elicited by negative versus neutral stimuli in alcoholic subjects compared with healthy volunteers.

spans.text: We tested the hypotheses that a high relapse risk is associated with (1) increased brain activation during the presentation of alcohol-associated versus neutral stimuli in the prefrontal and cingulate cortex, striatum, and visual association centers, (2) decreased brain activation elicited by positive versus neutral stimuli in the brain reward system, particularly the ventral striatum/nucleus accumbens, and (3) increased amygdala activation elicited by negative versus neutral stimuli in alcoholic subjects compared with healthy volunteers.
